- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast 2–3 periods ahead.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%; if below, increase by 5–10%.
- Model underperforms in early horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: average last 3 sentiment values to dampen noise.
